title: Aggrega Wasm Linter Socket
description: The JSON wire shapes the publishing-linter.wasm plugin socket consumes (LinterInput) and emits (LinterOutput). The linter runs at publish time over a previous-version + proposed-version entity pair (the schema-evolution rule) and at workspace lint time over individual entities (per-rule structural rules). One shipping Wasm plugin hosts many rules; the dispatcher selects which rule to run via the LinterInput.rule_id field. The two wire shapes are co-canonical with the corresponding PDK mirrors at aggrega-pdk/<lang>/src/types; per-language round-trip tests catch drift.

LinterInput.description: The payload the host hands the publishing-linter plugin on each invocation. rule_id selects which rule the plugin dispatches to. entity_kind identifies the entity kind being linted (Component, Feature, Recipe, FeatureRecipe, SchemaLibrary, MappingLibrary, Aggregate). proposed carries the parsed entity structure being classified (the host parses YAML to JSON before sending; the plugin never sees raw bytes). previous carries the parsed previous-version entity for the schema-evolution rule; omitted when not applicable. policies carries the per-workspace publishing-discipline configuration the rule consults.

rule_id.description: The rule the plugin should dispatch to. At v0.1.0 the only recognised value is 'schema-evolution'; the recognised set expands as further rules ship. Unknown rule_ids produce an 'unknown_rule' finding in the output.

entity_kind.description: The entity kind the proposed/previous values encode. The schema-evolution rule's classification varies per kind; structural rules scope to specific kinds.

proposed.description: Parsed structure of the entity being classified. YAML → JSON conversion happens host-side; the plugin consumes the structured value via serde_json.

previous.description: Parsed structure of the previous-version entity, for rules that perform pairwise comparison (schema-evolution). Omitted when the rule does not need a previous-version reference (e.g., first publication, structural-only rules).

parent.description: Parsed structure of the resolved parent entity in the extends chain, for rules that perform child-vs-parent comparison (narrowing). The host caller resolves the entity's spec.extends URI before invocation. Omitted when no parent exists or the rule does not need parent context.

source_path.description: Filesystem path the entity was loaded from. Populated by host callers walking the catalog filesystem; consumed by path-aware rules (e.g., category-matches-directory). Omitted when the caller has no path context.

policies.description: The per-workspace publishing-discipline configuration the rule consults. The guest realizes it as the typed Policies object; the host pipes it through as an opaque payload it assembles from the workspace config and CLI overrides.

LinterOutput.description: The response shape the publishing-linter plugin emits. findings carries one entry per rule invocation that produced a result. The schema-evolution rule emits exactly one finding (the classification verdict); structural rules may emit zero (no violations) or many (one per offence).

findings.description: Per-rule findings produced by the plugin invocation, in plugin emit order.

error.description: A failure message set when the guest ran but could not complete the operation; absent on success. It is distinct from any diagnostics the output carries: diagnostics report issues found during a run that still produced a result, while error reports that the operation itself did not complete. The host surfaces a present error as a failed plugin invocation.

Policies.description: Per-workspace publishing-discipline configuration the rule set consults. Mirrors workspaceconfig.PublishingDisciplineConfig field-for-field. Schema is the contract: both the Go workspaceconfig struct's godoc AND the Rust policies.rs struct doc cross-reference this $def. Field omission defaults each flag to false; the host's serialiser writes only fields with non-default values.

enforce_monotonic_narrowing.description: When true, the narrowing rule enforces the monotonic-narrowing invariant: every extending entity narrows the parent's schema (no widening, no semantic divergence). When false, the rule is suppressed.

enforce_immutability.description: When true, published artefacts are immutable at the registry path; re-publishing the same version is rejected. When false, the rule is suppressed (development-only).

narrowing_exemptions.description: Per-entity exemptions from the narrowing-violation rule. Each entry names an entity and the specific schema paths that may legitimately widen.

allow_dynamic_refs.description: When true, $dynamicAnchor / $dynamicRef usage in SchemaLibrary entries is permitted (suppresses the dynamic_refs rule). Default false.

allow_id_overrides.description: When true, $id overrides in SchemaLibrary entries are permitted (suppresses the id_overrides rule). Default false.

allow_direct_x_aggrega_extensions.description: When true, direct x-aggrega-selector / x-aggrega-inject authoring is permitted (suppresses the x_aggrega_discouragement rule). Default false.

allow_aggrega_ai_prefix.description: When true, the annotation-prefix rule is suppressed entirely (both the bare aggrega.ai/ check and the feature.aggrega.ai/ kind-conditional check). Default false. Mirrors workspaceconfig.PublishingDisciplineConfig.AllowAggregaAIPrefix; the host serialises the field through the LinterInput.policies passthrough.

allow_nonstandard_names.description: When true, name-shape violations are permitted (suppresses the name_shape rule). Default false.

allow_category_mismatches.description: When true, suppress the category-matches-directory rule's findings. The standard-catalog convention requires Components under core/<category>/ to declare component.aggrega.ai/category={category} matching the directory segment, where {category} is one of the 15 closed-set values. Workspaces with legitimate persistent exceptions opt out here. Default false.

NarrowingExemption.description: One per-entity exemption from the narrowing-violation rule. entity names the catalog entity; paths enumerates the schema paths within that entity that may legitimately widen; reason is the human-readable justification surfaced to reviewers.
